questions.question: Which processor architecture is described as using separate buses for instructions and data to achieve fast processing in DSP processors?
questions.explanation:
The text states that DSP processors should have a fast processing architecture and therefore use the Harvard Architecture with separate instruction and data buses. [Page 95]  

---

questions.question: According to the passage, what most clearly differentiates DSP chips from general‑purpose microprocessors?

options.A: They are built with vacuum‑tube technology.
options.B: They are specially designed for particular signal‑processing applications.
options.C: They use a single unified bus for all transfers.
options.D: They operate at higher clock frequencies than any microprocessor.

questions.explanation:
The context notes that DSP chips are specially designed for particular applications and are not used for the general type of processing that microprocessors perform. [Page 95]  

---

questions.question: Which set of hardware components is mentioned as being part of the overall function carried out by a DSP processor?

options.A: Microphone, transducer, A/D converter, D/A converter, speaker
options.C: Antenna, RF mixer, demodulator, antenna tuner

questions.explanation:
The passage lists microphone, transducer, A/D converter, D/A converter, and speaker as the hardware used with DSP processors. [Page 95]  

---

questions.question: Which software tools are identified in the text as being used to carry out the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) on a DSP processor?
questions.explanation:
The context states that software like C or MATLAB is used to carry out FFT on DSP processors. [Page 95]  

---

questions.question: What benefit of converting analog signals into digital signals is highlighted in the passage?

options.B: It makes the signal more immune to noise.
options.C: It eliminates the need for an ADC.

questions.explanation:
The text explains that converting analog signals into digital signals reduces redundancy and makes the signal more immune to noise. [Page 94]  

---

questions.question: Which DSP chip series from Texas Instruments is described as “worldwide popular”?
questions.explanation:
The passage notes that Texas Instruments’ TMS320C series is worldwide popular for signal‑processing applications. [Page 95]  

---

questions.question: In the DT/R (Data Transmit/Receive) signal description, what does a high level on this line indicate?

options.B: The processor is sending out data.
options.D: The processor is in reset state.

questions.explanation:
The text states that when the processor sends out data, the DT/R signal is high; when receiving, it is low. [Page 41]  

---

questions.question: Which conversion component is required to change the microphone’s analog output into a digital form suitable for the DSP processor?
questions.explanation:
The passage explains that the microphone’s analog signal is sampled by an A/D converter and then converted into digital form for the DSP. [Page 94]  

---

questions.question: According to the description of a bus in a microcomputer, which statement is true?

options.A: A bus consists of multiple communication lines capable of transmitting binary 0s and 1s.
options.B: A bus is a single wire that carries only analog signals.
options.C: A bus is used solely for delivering power to components.
options.D: A bus can transmit only one bit at a time.

questions.explanation:
The text defines a bus as a communication pathway composed of multiple lines, each capable of transmitting binary signals. [Page 42]  

---

questions.question: What limitation of DSP processors is mentioned in the material?

options.A: They have low processing speed because very short signals need to be operated.
options.B: They can only execute programs written in assembly language.
options.C: They are incapable of handling any real‑time data.
options.D: They require more than three separate power supplies.

questions.explanation: The passage notes that DSP processors have low processing speed due to the need to operate very curtail (short) signals. [Page 95]
